overviewHtml:
Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour

Experience the spectacular Himalayas on an Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour from Kathmandu, an unforgettable one-day adventure designed for travelers who want to explore the Everest region without completing a multi-day trek. Enjoy breathtaking aerial views of Mount Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, the Khumbu Glacier, and the surrounding Himalayan landscape.

Operated by Nepal Unique Treks, this helicopter sightseeing experience combines convenient airport transfers, a scenic flight through the Everest region, and planned stops subject to weather, safety, and operational conditions. Depending on the confirmed itinerary, you may also enjoy a stop at Hotel Everest View for breakfast with panoramic mountain views.

Whether you are visiting Nepal for a short holiday, celebrating a special occasion, or looking for a memorable Himalayan experience, our Everest helicopter tour offers a convenient way to discover the beauty of the world's highest mountain region.

  • Duration: Approximately 4–5 hours, subject to flight conditions
  • Departure: Kathmandu, Nepal
  • Tour type: Shared helicopter or private charter, subject to availability
  • Price: See the current group-size price table below

Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour Highlights

  • Experience a breathtaking scenic helicopter flight over the majestic Himalayas of Nepal.
  • Enjoy spectacular aerial views of Mount Everest (8,848.86 m), the world's highest mountain.
  • Witness panoramic views of Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, Pumori, and other towering Himalayan peaks.
  • Fly over the beautiful Khumbu region, surrounded by snow-capped mountains, glaciers, and deep valleys.
  • Enjoy stunning aerial views of the Khumbu Glacier and the dramatic Everest Base Camp area.
  • Land at Kala Patthar (subject to weather, altitude, and operational conditions) for unforgettable close-up views of Mount Everest.
  • Enjoy a memorable breakfast with spectacular Himalayan scenery at a high-altitude location, subject to the tour itinerary and operating conditions.
  • Admire traditional Sherpa villages, monasteries, and the unique culture of the Everest region.
  • Capture incredible photographs and videos of the world's most iconic mountain landscapes.
  • Experience the beauty of the Everest region in a single day without the physical demands of a multi-day trek.
  • Enjoy a convenient and time-efficient Himalayan adventure with an experienced helicopter crew.
  • Create unforgettable memories of Nepal's magnificent mountains on this extraordinary Everest helicopter tour.

Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour Cost

The cost of an Everest Base Camp helicopter tour in Nepal depends on the type of tour, number of passengers, landing locations, season, and whether you choose a shared or private charter.
For travelers departing from Kathmandu, the tour typically includes a scenic flight over the Everest region, spectacular Himalayan views, and, on selected itineraries, a landing near Everest for photographs or breakfast.

  • Shared Helicopter Tour: Per Person US$1495
  • Private Helicopter Tour: US$ 5500

Best Time for an Everest Helicopter Tour

The two prime windows

  • October to November (post-monsoon) is generally the best. Skies are clear, the air is crisp, and visibility is at its peak. You’re in Kathmandu right now, and it’s mid-October, so you’re at the start of this window.
  • March to May (pre-monsoon) is the second best. Mornings are usually clear, though haze can build in the afternoons, especially in April and May.

Seasons to approach with caution

June to September (monsoon): Heavy cloud and rain make flights unreliable, and views are often blocked. Cancellations are common.
December to February (winter): Skies can be very clear, and it is less crowded, but it is cold and high winds can disrupt flights. Landings at Kala Patthar are colder and more demanding.

Time of day

Early morning (roughly 6 to 9 am) is the best. Clouds tend to build up in the valleys by late morning, so most operators fly early.

Practical tips

Build in a spare day if you can, since weather cancellations are common even in peak season.
Book a few days ahead rather than far in advance, so you can pick a day with a good forecast.
Peak season means higher demand, so check availability early with your operator.

Safety, Altitude, and Landing Information

Altitude

  • Kathmandu is about 1,400 m, so you start already slightly acclimatized compared to sea level.
  • Syangboche / Everest View Hotel (about 3,800 m) is a gentle landing. Most people feel fine, though a mild headache is possible.
  • Kala Patthar (about 5,500 m) is where the air has roughly half the oxygen of sea level. Landings are kept short, usually just a few minutes, because you haven’t acclimatized.
  • Symptoms of altitude sickness include headache, nausea, dizziness, and unusual breathlessness. If you feel unwell, tell the crew right away. Descent is the cure, and helicopters make that quick.

Who should be cautious

  • People with heart or lung conditions, high blood pressure, or recent illness should check with a doctor before booking.
  • Pregnancy, severe anemia, and uncontrolled asthma are also reasons to get medical advice first.
  • Moving slowly, drinking water, and avoiding alcohol the day before all help.

Landing realities

  • Landings at high altitude are demanding for helicopters, since thin air reduces lift. Operators limit passenger numbers and fuel loads accordingly.
  • Landing spots can change based on wind, weather, and permissions on the day. A landing is never guaranteed.
  • Many itineraries offer a no-landing option that flies close to the peaks and may suit you better if you’re unsure about altitude.

Operator and aircraft safety

  • Fly with a licensed operator approved by Nepal’s Civil Aviation Authority (CAAN) and registered with a recognized tourism body, such as the Nepal Tourism Board.
  • Ask about the helicopter type (twin-engine aircraft are common for high-altitude work), pilot experience in the Himalaya, and maintenance practices.
  • Check that the operator has insurance and emergency evacuation procedures.
  • Nepal’s mountain weather changes quickly, and good operators will cancel or divert rather than push through poor conditions. Treat a cancellation as a safety feature, not a failure.

Before you go

  • Confirm that your travel insurance covers helicopter flights and high-altitude activity. Some policies exclude it or need an add-on.
  • Carry any personal medication, and wear layers, sunglasses, and sunscreen. UV is intense at altitude.
  • Listen carefully to the safety briefing, especially on rotor clearance and approaching the aircraft.

itinerary.title: One Day Itinerary for the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Day Tours
itinerary.description: Drive to the Airport Your day starts at around 5:00 A.M., as you need to wake up and freshen up yourself before checking the backpack for the final time. At 5:30 A.M., the representatives from Nepal Unique Treks will pick you up in a private vehicle and drive you to the Tribhuwan International Airport. The bus vehicle will directly drop you off at the domestic terminals of the airport. As the streets are quiet and free from traffic jams, it won't take much time to reach the airport from the hotel. Take off from the Tribhuwan International Airport As you arrive at the Airport and go for some essential checking after which you will have the boarding pass in your hands. After that, the visitors will be taken to the helicopter and carefully settled by the staff. Within a few minutes, the helicopter takes off into the clouds. The flight ascends toward the east, following the legendary Jiri route, weaving through alpine forests and traditional villages, offering a mesmerizing contrast of green hills and towering white peaks. Landing in Lukla - The Gateway to Everest Within about 30 hours of scenic and luxurious flight over the valleys, cities, forests, etc, the helicopter lands at the Tenzing & Hilary Airport (Lukla). This landing is necessary during the EBC Heli Tour for the helicopter to refuel. In the meantime, travelers can experience the cool breeze coming straight from the Himalayas. A little while ago, you were in a hustling and bustling capital city of Nepal, and within just 30 minutes, you reached a peaceful and quiet place. Therefore, take your time to admire the dramatic scenery offered by Lukla. Once the helicopter is fueled up and ready to go; that's when the real adventure begins. From there, we will fly towards the Everest Base camp. Flying Over Everest Base Camp and Landing at Kalapatthar As the helicopter lifts off from Lukla, you can see that the landscape transforms into a world of ice, rock, and towering Himalayas. Furthermore, you will also witness the massive Khumbu Glacier along with several peaks, including Ama Dablam, Lhotse, Nuptse, and Pumori. A little later, the helicopter will be hovering over the Everest Base Camp (5364 meters). Make sure that you look below to see many trekkers and summiteers walking on the Base Camp. Moreover, there will also be many tents settled by the climbers to rest in the Everest Base Camp before summiting the Everest Peak (8850 meters). After that, the helicopter lands on the Kalapatthar viewpoint (5550 meters), where you will get off and enjoy the views for a while. As you step onto the rocky terrain, the sheer magnitude of the mountains surrounding you is overwhelming. Besides, the cold, thin air carries a sense of reverence, and for 10 to 15 minutes, you stand face-to-face with Everest. Let us tell you that this will probably be the best experience for any visitors. Breakfast with a View at the Everest View Hotel After taking some amazing glimpses of Mount Everest, surrounding peaks, and valleys from the Kalapatthar viewpoint, the visitors will board the helicopter again. From there, the helicopter takes you to the Everest View Hotel, the hotel located at the highest altitude of 3,880 meters above sea level. Here, you enjoy a hearty breakfast, sipping warm tea as the sunlight dances over the snow-covered peaks. Along with that, the Everest View Hotel also offers mesmerizing panoramic views of the Himalayas. Return to Lukla & Kathmandu With that breakfast getting over, we almost come to the end of this one-day Helicopter Tour to the Everest Base Camp. After breakfast, you will board the helicopter and go for a quick flight to Lukla. Just like it happened in the arriving journey, the helicopter takes a refueling break in Lukla (Tenzing & Hilary Airport). After the refueling is done, the visitors will be flown to Kathmandu which takes about half an hour. By 11:00 AM, you’re back in the bustling streets of Kathmandu, yet a part of you still lingers in the mountains. This officially puts an end to the adventurous Everest Base Camp Helicopter Day Tour.

usefulInfoHtml:
Traveller Useful Information

For a Day tour via helicopter, we might think any season throughout the year might be perfect. However, to get an unobstructed aerial view during the flight, we need to choose the right season and fly in a perfect weather condition. Moreover, clear skies, stable weather, and breathtaking views make spring and autumn the best times for this adventure.

Spring(March to May) offers vibrant landscapes, blooming rhododendrons, and crystal-clear mountain views. Mornings are generally bright, and the weather remains stable. The Himalayas stand majestic against a deep blue sky. However, this is a peak season, so expect some crowding at landing spots.

Autumn (September to November) is another ideal time, bringing crisp air, mild temperatures, and excellent visibility. The monsoon clears away dust, leaving the skies exceptionally clear. Snow-capped peaks and golden hills create a stunning contrast. This season also attracts many travelers, so booking in advance is wise.

Winter (December to February) flights offer breathtaking, snow-covered scenery and clear skies, but temperatures can be freezing. The helicopter tour is still possible. However, the weather conditions can affect the regular flights. Fewer tourists mean a quieter experience.

Monsoon (June to Early September) is the least favorable season due to heavy rainfall, clouds, and unpredictable weather. Flight delays and cancellations are common. If you plan a trip during this time, flexibility is essential.

  • Enjoy the breathtaking views, but always prioritize safety first!

  • Fasten your seat belt securely once seated in the helicopter.

  • Do not change your seat or stand up during the flight. Sudden movements can affect balance.

  • Never throw anything out of the helicopter, as it can be hazardous to people and the environment.

  • Smoking is strictly prohibited inside the helicopter.

  • Wait at the helipad until the crew calls you to board. Always follow their instructions.

  • Approach and exit the helicopter from the designated side, as directed by the pilot.

  • Keep loose items like scarves, hats, and bags secured to prevent them from being blown away.

  • High-altitude conditions can be extreme. Stay hydrated and inform the crew if you feel unwell.

  • Listen carefully to the safety briefing before takeoff. Your safety depends on following instructions.

  • Enjoy the breathtaking views, but always prioritize safety first!

Even though it is a 1-day tour on a helicopter flight, we still require some necessary items with us in the Himalayas. Below are the items that we need to pack for Everest Base Camp Helicopter Day Tour:

  • Windproof and waterproof jacket

  • Layered clothing

  • Warm hat and gloves

  • UV-protection sunglasses

  • Sturdy hiking boots or warm sneakers

  • Thermal socks

  • Valid passport

  • Small backpack

  • Camera or smartphone

  • Extra batteries and power bank

  • Snacks and energy bars

  • Sunscreen and lip balm (SPF 50+)

  • Water bottle with purification tablets

  • Personal medications

  • Small first-aid kit

  • Optional oxygen canister

  • Cash (Nepali Rupees)

  • Notebook and pen

  • Hand warmers

Tips: Dress in layers, pack light, and charge devices before the trip.

Note: The above gear will be sufficient for the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour. We encourage carrying only necessary equipment because over-carrying might increase the weight.

Regarding the booking process for this journey, we have multiple options. You can directly message us on WhatsApp, Zalo, or Viber at +9779851023285. Also, you can email us at info@nepaluniquetreks.com or nepaluniquetreks@gmail.com. Moreover, we also customize the itinerary according to your requirements and make sure your trip goes according to your plan.

After you choose how you want to proceed with the itinerary, for the booking we require a 30% deposit to secure your spot. In addition, you can communicate with our team directly regarding payment methods.

Once your booking is confirmed, we will provide you with additional information to help you prepare for your trip. If you have any questions about the booking process, feel free to contact us anytime.

  • A chance to witness the tallest mountain in the world within a day via a helicopter flight. Indulge yourself into experiencing the aerial of the mountain peaks, terrains, glaciers, lush hills, and many more in the journey.

  • Landing at one of the world's most adventurous airports, surrounded by dramatic mountain landscapes.

  • Witness breathtaking aerial views of mountain peaks, including Everest, Nuptse, and Ama Dablam, while flying over the stunning Khumbu Glacier.

  • The scenic views of the hills, glaciers, and diverse flora and fauna from the sky, capture the region’s natural beauty from the flight.

  • Perfect for those with limited time, this helicopter tour lets you experience the beauty of Everest without the need for a long trek.

liveFaqs.question: What is the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour?
liveFaqs.answer: The Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour is a 1-Day tour that flies you from Kathmandu to Everest Base Camp and back, offering stunning views of the Himalayas, including Mount Everest.

liveFaqs.question: How long does the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour take?
liveFaqs.answer: The tour typically takes 4 to 5 hours in total. Kathmandu Domestic Airport to Airport

liveFaqs.question: Where does the helicopter tour start and end?
liveFaqs.answer: The tour starts and ends at the Kathmandu domestic airport. But we Nepal Unique Treks driver pickup from your Hotel and drop off to the your Hotel.

liveFaqs.question: What is the maximum altitude reached during the tour?
liveFaqs.answer: The maximum altitude reached is 5,464 meters (Everest Base Camp/Kalapathar).

liveFaqs.question: What are the highlights of the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour?
liveFaqs.answer: Highlights include a scenic helicopter flight over the Himalayas, landing at the Everest View Hotel for breakfast, and seeing panoramic views of Mt. Everest, Khumbu Icefall, glaciers, and other peaks.

liveFaqs.question: What mountains can I see during the helicopter tour?
liveFaqs.answer: You can see Mt. Everest, Mt. Nuptse, Mt. Lhotse, Mt. Cho Oyu, Mt. Ama Dablam, Mt. Thamserku, Island Peak, Mt. Kongde, Mt. Pumori, and many other mountains.

liveFaqs.question: Is it possible to land at Everest Base Camp?
liveFaqs.answer: Due to government regulations, direct landings at Kalapatthar (near Everest Base Camp) are temporarily prohibited. The itinerary may be modified to include a stopover at Lukla instead.

liveFaqs.question: Where does the helicopter land during the tour?
liveFaqs.answer: The helicopter typically lands at Lukla for refueling, at the Everest View Hotel for breakfast, and potentially at Kalapatthar (depending on current regulations).

liveFaqs.question: How many people can the helicopter accommodate?
liveFaqs.answer: The helicopter can accommodate up to 5 people. Don't worry if you have only a few people we can adjust with another group (Join) Everest Base Camp Helicopter Day Tour

liveFaqs.question: What is the best time to take the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour?
liveFaqs.answer: Spring and Autumn are suggested as the best seasons for better views.

liveFaqs.question: How much does the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour cost?
liveFaqs.answer: The cost varies depending on the group size, ranging from USD 1250 to USD 1300 per person for a shared tour. Private tours are also available at a higher cost. Refer to the provided cost table for more details.

liveFaqs.question: Is there a refund policy if the flight is canceled due to bad weather?
liveFaqs.answer: Yes, a 100% full refund is guaranteed if no flight is made due to bad weather.

liveFaqs.question: What is the Everest View Hotel?
liveFaqs.answer: The Everest View Hotel is the highest-located deluxe hotel in the world, offering panoramic views of the Everest Region Himalayas. It is a stop on the tour for breakfast.

liveFaqs.question: What is the itinerary of the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour?
liveFaqs.answer: The general itinerary includes: hotel pickup, flight to Lukla, flying over Everest Base Camp, landing at Everest View Hotel for breakfast, and return flight to Kathmandu. See the "Day to Day Itinerary" section for more details.

liveFaqs.question: Are there alternative tour options available?
liveFaqs.answer: Yes, alternative options include combining the helicopter tour with a trek to Everest Base Camp (Heli Out or Luxury Trek with Helicopter Return). Regular Everest Base Camp Treks are also available.

liveFaqs.question: How do I book the Everest Base Camp Helicopter Tour?
liveFaqs.answer: You can contact Nepal Unique Treks via email or WhatsApp to check availability and book the tour.

liveFaqs.question: What is the cancelation policy?
liveFaqs.answer: If you cancel the booking less than two weeks in advance, you are subject to a charge of 20% of the total fare.
